# Custom Lab Themes

## Concept

Any organization can use the SWAPPS Design System with its own branding. The system does not hardcode any laboratory's styling into shared components.

Laboratory branding is separated from functional semantics:

- **Brand colors** affect general UI components (headers, navigation, toolbars).
- **Status colors** for controls and charts remain fixed regardless of the selected laboratory.
- **Light/dark mode** is shared across all components and all laboratories.

## Setting up a custom lab theme

### 1. Define your configuration

```tsx
import type { SWAPPSThemeConfig } from '@swapps/ui';

const myLabTheme: SWAPPSThemeConfig = {
  appearance: 'light',
  branding: {
    organizationName: 'Berkeley Lab',
    logoUrl: '/assets/lbnl-logo.svg',
    primaryColor: '#003262',
    accentColor: '#3B7EA1',
  },
};
```

### 2. Wrap your application

```tsx
import { SWAPPSThemeProvider, AppHeader } from '@swapps/ui';

function BerkeleyLabApp() {
  return (
    <SWAPPSThemeProvider config={myLabTheme}>
      <AppHeader appTitle="Detector Monitor" />
      <main id="main-content">
        {/* Application content */}
      </main>
    </SWAPPSThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

### 3. Components inherit automatically

- `AppHeader` displays **[Berkeley Lab]** with the configured logo.
- General UI elements pick up `--swapps-brand-primary` and `--swapps-brand-accent`.
- Scientific controls use the standard status palette — not your brand colors.
- Charts use the standard visualization palette.

## What branding affects

| Component category | Organization name | Logo | Brand colors | Status colors | Chart palette |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| General UI | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Standard | Standard |
| Controls | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | Standard | Standard |
| Charts | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | Standard | Standard |

## Try it in the documentation

Use the [interactive configurator](/docs/themes/overview) to:

1. Enter your organization name and brand colors.
2. Preview how the AppHeader and other components look.
3. Copy the generated configuration for use in your application.

The exported configuration uses the same `SWAPPSThemeConfig` schema that your application code expects.

## Ensuring accessible brand colors

When choosing brand colors, verify that they provide sufficient contrast for their intended use:

- **Header backgrounds**: White text on brand primary should meet WCAG AA for large text (3:1 ratio).
- **Accent links/buttons**: Ensure adequate contrast against the page background.

The theme configurator shows contrast validation badges next to configured colors. The `meetsWCAG_AA` utility can be used programmatically:

```tsx
import { meetsWCAG_AA } from '@swapps/ui';

const isAccessible = meetsWCAG_AA('#ffffff', '#003262', true);
// true — white text on Berkeley Lab blue passes AA for large text
```

## Important notes

- Sample colors in documentation are illustrative only — they do not represent official colors of any organization.
- Brand colors do not override Carbon semantic tokens (`$support-error`, `$support-warning`, etc.).
- The same component can be used across multiple laboratories — only the configuration changes.
